records.title: Type A and Type B describe evaluation methods
records.text: Type A uses statistical evaluation; Type B uses other information. These categories do not map one-to-one onto random and systematic effects.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Do not classify an effect solely by whether it appears random or systematic.

records.title: Standard uncertainty
records.text: Standard uncertainty represents an uncertainty component as an estimated standard deviation.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: This reference is not a laboratory calibration or independent replication.

records.title: Error is not uncertainty
records.text: A result can have a small unknown error yet substantial uncertainty. Uncertainty is not the realized error.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: The true error is generally not known from an uncertainty estimate.

records.title: Type A methods beyond repeated means
records.text: Type A evaluations can use valid statistical analyses such as least squares or analysis of variance, not only repeated-reading means.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: The appropriate statistical design depends on the measurement process.

records.title: Uncertainty of a repeated-reading mean
records.text: For independent observations under the same conditions, estimate the mean uncertainty from their sample dispersion.
assumptions: n >= 2 independent observations under the same measurement conditions.
limitations: Autocorrelation and drift can invalidate this calculation.

records.title: First-order uncertainty propagation
records.text: Combine input variances and covariances using local sensitivities.
assumptions: First-order Taylor approximation; sensitivities evaluated at input estimates.
limitations: Nonlinearity may require another method.

records.title: Correlated measurement inputs
records.text: Covariance terms contribute to the combined variance when inputs are correlated.
assumptions: Covariance estimates describe the joint input uncertainty.
limitations: Zero correlation must not be silently inferred from missing metadata.

records.title: Uncertainty of a difference
records.text: Substituting sensitivities +1 and -1 gives the variance of a difference.
assumptions: Both inputs describe comparable quantities in compatible units.
limitations: No acceptance decision follows without a declared decision rule.

records.title: Type B information sources
records.text: Type B evaluation may use previous data, specifications, calibration reports, experience, and reference information.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: A source must be relevant to the actual measurement conditions.

records.title: Uniform bounded uncertainty
records.text: For a symmetric uniform model with half-width a, the standard uncertainty is a divided by sqrt(3).
assumptions: Equal probability within justified symmetric bounds.
limitations: Bounds alone do not establish a uniform distribution.

records.title: Triangular bounded uncertainty
records.text: For a symmetric triangular model with half-width a, use a divided by sqrt(6).
assumptions: A symmetric triangular probability model is justified.
limitations: Do not select this model merely to obtain a smaller uncertainty.

records.title: Convert a reported uncertainty multiplier
records.text: Divide an uncertainty stated as a multiple of a standard deviation by its stated multiplier.
assumptions: The report supplies the multiplier and meaning of U.
limitations: A missing multiplier cannot be guessed.

records.title: Corrections for systematic effects
records.text: Recognized significant systematic effects should be corrected where possible; the correction carries its own uncertainty.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: The uncertainty of a correction is not the systematic error itself.

records.title: Combine Type A and Type B components
records.text: Components from either evaluation method enter a combined standard uncertainty with covariance where appropriate.
assumptions: Components use standard uncertainties and a defensible measurement model.
limitations: This reference is not a laboratory calibration or independent replication.

records.title: Expanded uncertainty
records.text: Expanded uncertainty multiplies combined standard uncertainty by a chosen coverage factor.
assumptions: Coverage factor k is explicit and justified.
limitations: Multiplication alone does not establish a coverage probability.

records.title: Coverage factor is not a universal probability
records.text: A factor of two corresponds to approximately 95 percent coverage under the stated normal-distribution and negligible-uncertainty conditions.
assumptions: Normal approximation applies and uncertainty in u_c is negligible for that interpretation.
limitations: Do not label every k=2 interval as 95 percent.

records.title: Report uncertainty with its basis
records.text: Report components, their evaluation methods, and the coverage factor when expanded uncertainty is used. State the basis of any probability interpretation.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Keep referenced measurement procedures consistent with the process used.

records.title: Traceability belongs to a measurement result
records.text: Metrological traceability relates a measurement result to a reference through a documented calibration chain with uncertainty contributions.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: An instrument calibration by itself does not establish traceability of every subsequent result.

records.title: Traceability documentation requirements
records.text: Document the measurand, measurement system, result and uncertainty, reference calibration, and relevant measurement assurance.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Checking graph links cannot authenticate certificates or establish competence.

records.title: Traceability is not fitness for purpose
records.text: A traceable result can still be unsuitable for an application when its uncertainty is too large.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Application requirements must be evaluated separately.
